draft.title: Classifying quadrilaterals
card: A quadrilateral has 4 straight sides. Shapes are told apart by their parallel sides, equal sides, angles and diagonals (lines joining opposite corners).
A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. Its opposite sides are equal and its opposite angles are equal.
A rectangle is a parallelogram with four right angles, and its diagonals are equal. A rhombus is a parallelogram with four equal sides, and its diagonals cross at right angles.
A square has four equal sides and four right angles. A trapezium has at least one pair of parallel sides. A kite has two pairs of equal sides that sit next to each other.
draft.remember: Sort quadrilaterals by asking about parallel sides, equal sides, angles and diagonals.

a.q: A quadrilateral has two pairs of parallel sides and four equal sides, but no right angles. What is its most exact name?
a.why: Two pairs of parallel sides make it a parallelogram, and four equal sides make it a rhombus. A square also has four equal sides, but it needs four right angles, and this shape has none.
a.clue: Check the angles before choosing between rhombus and square.

b.q: Priya draws a quadrilateral with four right angles. It has two long sides and two short sides, and each long side is opposite the other. What is it?
b.why: Four right angles and two pairs of parallel, equal opposite sides make it a rectangle. A square is tempting because of the right angles, but a square needs four equal sides, and these sides are not all equal. A kite needs equal sides next to each other, and this shape has none.
